You are helping in a project that uses the Taproot design system. Its packages are installed in node_modules. Its CLI is at node_modules/.bin/taproot, and `node_modules/.bin/taproot help agents` explains how to use it.

Build the page as one HTML file named index.html in the current directory, with Taproot's web components. There is no bundler: load what the page needs from node_modules. Write the components as markup in the HTML, not from script. When the file is written, reply with one line saying so.

Build a profile form in the state after a save attempt failed. A message at the top of the form says the changes were not saved because the connection dropped, with a Try again action. The form has Name and Email fields and a Save button. The email field holds 'sam@' and shows what to fix.

The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY). A component's
  rules include those of the patterns and guidelines it follows, at their own addresses (for
  example `pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit`).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names. Once per project, read `setup --impl <name>` (MCP: `setup`)
  for what every component shares: installing the package, loading its styles, and fonts.
- Components style only themselves. Before building a page, `get guideline.page-setup` for the
  page's base font, text color, background, and heading recipes, and load the base stylesheet it
  names when your technology has one.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

content:
# Web components setup

What every web component needs, once per project. Each component's own file in this folder maps its
API; `taproot setup --impl web` prints this one.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @taproot-ds/web-components @taproot-ds/tokens
```

## Load the styles

Load the token stylesheet once, at the application root, before any component renders. Without it,
the components have no colors, spacing, or type. The optional base stylesheet styles the page
around them: the base font, text color, background, and a type recipe for each heading level
(`guideline.page-setup`). The components style only themselves.

```js
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/base"; // optional page defaults
```

Without a bundler, link the files from the tokens package instead:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/base.css" />
```

The components read semantic tokens directly, so they follow the active theme. With no
`data-theme` on the root element, the theme follows the system preference; `data-theme="light"` or
`"dark"` overrides it. The tokens a component reads are not a customization API.

## Fonts

The font tokens name Lora, Source Sans 3, and JetBrains Mono, with system fallbacks. The packages do
not ship the font files. The tokens package's readme has the links to load them.

## Register the elements

Import the package root once to register every element under its `ds-` tag:

```js
import "@taproot-ds/web-components";
```

Or import one component's module and call its define function, as each component's Import section
shows. A define function takes another tag name when `ds-` names collide.

The modules are standard ES modules with no runtime dependencies. Without a bundler, map the bare
package names with an import map, or import the files under `node_modules/@taproot-ds/web-components/src/`.

content:
$ taproot get guideline.page-setup
# Page setup

Set the page's base font, text color, background, and heading type from semantic tokens, because components style only themselves.

The components style only themselves. The page around them, the text between them, and the
headings above them get no style from any component. Without these defaults, components look right
while the page around them falls back to the platform's serif font and plain white, and nothing
reports the gap.

## What the page sets

| Page element | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `semantic.color.background.default` | The page itself. Raised areas use `semantic.color.background.surface`. |
| Base text | `semantic.typography.body.md` | Font family, size, weight, line height, and letter spacing. |
| Text color | `semantic.color.foreground.default` | Supporting text uses `semantic.color.foreground.muted`. |
| Small print | `semantic.typography.body.sm` | Captions and fine print. |
| Page title (level 1) | `semantic.typography.heading.lg` | One per page. |
| Section heading (level 2) | `semantic.typography.heading.md` | |
| Subsection heading (level 3) | `semantic.typography.heading.sm` | The recipe Card uses for its title. |
| Deeper headings (levels 4 to 6) | `semantic.typography.title` | The bold sans title Alert and Dialog use. |
| Code | `semantic.typography.code.md` | Inline code and code blocks. |
| Eyebrow above a heading | `semantic.typography.eyebrow` | A short category line, not a heading. |

A typography token such as `semantic.typography.body.md` is a recipe: it groups a font family,
size, weight, line height, and letter spacing, and each is its own token
(`semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily`). Set all five together. Mixing parts of two recipes
produces a size and line height that were never designed together.

For the values in each theme, read the token package, or resolve a component that uses the
recipe, such as `taproot tokens card --part title --resolve`.

## Token names in your technology

A token reference such as `semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily` is technology-neutral. Each
technology's token package publishes it under its own name, and that package says how. In the web
package, a reference becomes a CSS custom property: prefix `--ds-`, join the segments with hyphens,
and turn camel case into hyphenated words, so the reference above is
`--ds-semantic-typography-body-md-font-family`. Check a name against the package's stylesheet
before you rely on it (`no-guessed-names`).

## Fonts

The font tokens name the system's typefaces with fallbacks. The token package does not ship the
font files. Load the typefaces the way your platform does, before the page renders; the token
package's readme lists them and gives the web links to load them. Without them, the fallbacks keep the page readable but it does not
look like the system.

## Theme

The token package follows the reader's light or dark preference, and lets the page choose one
instead. Set the theme at the root of the page so the background, the base text, and every
component change together. A part of the page that sets its own colors without semantic tokens
does not change with them.

## Spacing and layout

Lay out the page with the spacing primitives, `primitives.space.*`, and put product layout
between components rather than inside them (`guideline.compose-or-propose`). The system has no
grid, container, or page template component; compose those in product code.

## Rules

### Behavior

- **MUST** load-tokens: Load the token package once, at the root of the page, before any component renders. Without it, components have no colors, spacing, or type.
- **MUST** page-base-text: The page's base text uses the body recipe, `semantic.typography.body.md`, in `semantic.color.foreground.default`. Text the components do not draw would otherwise fall back to the platform's default font and color.
- **MUST** page-background: The page background is `semantic.color.background.default`, so it follows the active theme with the components on it.
- **SHOULD** heading-recipes: Each heading level uses a heading recipe: the page title `semantic.typography.heading.lg`, section headings `semantic.typography.heading.md`, subsection headings `semantic.typography.heading.sm`, and deeper levels `semantic.typography.title`. Choose the level by the document outline, and the recipe by the level.
- **SHOULD** base-stylesheet: Where the token package offers a base stylesheet for your technology, load it rather than writing the page defaults by hand. It applies these rules with names that are already right. `taproot setup --impl <name>` names it for each implementation.
- **MUST** no-guessed-names: Take each token's name in your technology from the token package or a lookup, never from a guess. A misspelled token name fails silently and the platform default shows instead.

## Links

### related

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

$ taproot get alert --impl web
# Alert

Use Alert for a short status message in the flow of the page, announced only when you ask.

Shows a short status message, with an optional title, icon, actions, and dismiss control, in the flow of the surrounding content. It is announced to assistive technology only when its announce parameter asks for it.

## When to use

- Report the outcome of something the person just did, such as a saved form or a failed upload.
- Warn about a condition that affects the current view, such as an expiring session.
- Explain why part of the view is unavailable, with an action that resolves it.

## When not to use

- Label a status or category on an item in a list or table. Use [Badge](component.badge) instead. Badge is a compact label on an item. Alert is a message in the flow of the page.
- Ask for a decision before the person can continue. Use [Dialog](component.dialog) instead. Alert does not block the view or hold focus. Dialog does.
- Report a problem with one field's value. Instead: The field's own error message. Field errors belong next to the field, associated with it.
- Show a message that disappears on its own after a few seconds. Instead: A persistent Alert the person dismisses. A timed message can vanish before someone has read it.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| surface | container | Bounded message surface whose color and border follow the variant. |
| icon | indicator | Optional supplied graphic that reinforces the variant. |
| title | label | Optional short title that names the status. |
| message | description | The status message itself. |
| actions | container | Optional supplied actions that respond to the message. |
| dismiss | interactive-surface | Optional control that dismisses the alert. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | enum | `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `info` |  |
...

3	
4	Use Alert for a short status message in the flow of the page, announced only when you ask.
5	
6	Shows a short status message, with an optional title, icon, actions, and dismiss control, in the flow of the surrounding content. It is announced to assistive technology only when its announce parameter asks for it.
7	
8	## When to use
9	
10	- Report the outcome of something the person just did, such as a saved form or a failed upload.
11	- Warn about a condition that affects the current view, such as an expiring session.
12	- Explain why part of the view is unavailable, with an action that resolves it.
13	
14	## When not to use
15	
16	- Label a status or category on an item in a list or table. Use [Badge](component.badge) instead. Badge is a compact label on an item. Alert is a message in the flow of the page.
17	- Ask for a decision before the person can continue. Use [Dialog](component.dialog) instead. Alert does not block the view or hold focus. Dialog does.
18	- Report a problem with one field's value. Instead: The field's own error message. Field errors belong next to the field, associated with it.
19	- Show a message that disappears on its own after a few seconds. Instead: A persistent Alert the person dismisses. A timed message can vanish before someone has read it.
20	
21	## Anatomy
22	
23	| Part | Role | Description |
24	| --- | --- | --- |
25	| surface | container | Bounded message surface whose color and border follow the variant. |
26	| icon | indicator | Optional supplied graphic that reinforces the variant. |
27	| title | label | Optional short title that names the status. |
28	| message | description | The status message itself. |
29	| actions | container | Optional supplied actions that respond to the message. |
30	| dismiss | interactive-surface | Optional control that dismisses the alert. |
31	
32	## Parameters
33	
34	| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
35	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
36	| variant | enum | `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `info` |  |
37	| announce | enum | `off`, `polite`, `urgent` | `off` |  |
38	
39	`variant` values:
40	
41	- `info`: Neutral information or a change that needs no action. Example: A new version is available.
42	- `success`: Something completed as intended. Example: Your changes were saved.
43	- `warning`: A condition that needs attention but does not block the person. Example: Your session expires in 5 minutes.
44	- `danger`: Something failed or is blocked. Example: The upload failed. Check your connection and try again.
45	
46	`announce` values:
47	
48	- `off`: Shown without being announced. For messages present when the view loads. Example: A new version is available.
49	- `polite`: Announced when the person is not busy, without interrupting current speech. Example: Your changes were saved.
50	- `urgent`: Announced immediately, interrupting current speech. Example: Your session expires in 1 minute.
51	
52	## Events
53	
54	- `dismiss`: The dismiss control was activated. Preventing the event keeps the alert shown.
55	
56	## Parts
57	
58	### title
59	
60	Options of the `title` part.
61	
62	| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
63	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
64	| label | string |  |  | Optional text shown as the title part, read before the message. |
65	
66	### dismiss
67	
68	Options of the `dismiss` part.
69	
70	| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
71	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
72	| dismissible | boolean |  | `false` | Whether the alert shows a control that dismisses it. |
73	| dismissLabel | string |  | `Dismiss` | Accessible name of the dismiss control. Translate it with the rest of the interface. |
74	
75	## States
76	
77	`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `pressed`
78	
79	## Rules
80	
81	Includes the rules of guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown.
82	
83	### Content
84	
85	- **SHOULD** urgent-sparingly: Use urgent only for time-sensitive information the person must act on now. Most outcomes are polite.
86	  - Do: Urgent: Your session expires in 1 minute.; Polite: Your changes were saved.
87	  - Avoid: Urgent: A new version is available.
88	- **SHOULD** off-when-present-on-load: Leave announce off for an alert that is part of the view when it loads. People find it while reading, and announcing it competes with the page itself.
89	- **SHOULD** dismiss-only-when-safe: Do not make an alert dismissible while its condition still needs action. Dismissing a blocking error hides the reason something cannot continue.
90	- **SHOULD** keep-message-short: Keep the message to one or two sentences that say what happened and what to do next.
91	- **SHOULD** actions-follow-hierarchy: Offer at most two actions, and assign their emphasis by importance. Routine actions use low emphasis so they do not compete with the page's primary action.
92	  - See: pattern.action-hierarchy#assign-emphasis
93	
94	### Behavior
95	
96	- **MUST** announce-independent-of-variant: The variant never changes whether or how urgently the alert is announced.
97	- **MUST** no-focus-on-appear: Appearing or announcing never moves focus.
98	- **MUST** dismiss-reports: Activating the dismiss control reports dismiss. Unless the event is prevented, the alert then hides. Escape does not dismiss an alert.
99	- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
100	  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.
101	
102	### Accessibility
103	
104	- **MUST** text-states-status: The title or message states the status in words. Meaning never depends on the variant color or the icon alone.
105	  - Do: Upload failed: the file is larger than 10 MB.
106	  - Avoid: A red alert that only says the file name
107	- **MUST** announce-on-request: With announce off, appearing or changing does not announce the alert. With polite or urgent, the title and message are announced, with the matching urgency, when the alert appears and when that text changes. Actions and the dismiss control are not part of the announcement.
108	- **MUST** focus-after-dismiss: When the alert hides while it contains focus, focus moves to the next focusable item after the alert, or the previous one when nothing follows. A consumer handling dismiss may move focus elsewhere first.
109	- **MUST** dismiss-accessible-name: The dismiss control has an accessible name, from the dismiss label parameter.
110	- **SHOULD** icon-decorative-when-stated: Leave the icon unlabeled when the text already states the status.
111	  - See: component.icon#no-name-when-repeated
112	- **MUST** visible-focus: Keyboard focus on the dismiss control is visibly indicated on every variant.
113	  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#visible-focus
114	  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.
115	- **MUST** forced-colors: Under forced colors, the alert boundary and the dismiss control's focus stay visible.
116	  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors
117	- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone: Meaning never depends on color alone. Text, shape, or position carries it too.
118	
119	## Accessibility
120	
121	- Role: The title and message are an alert when announce is urgent and a status when polite. With announce off they have no role and read in place. Actions and the dismiss control sit outside the announced content.
122	- Name: None. The title and message are announced as content. The dismiss control is named by the dismiss label.
123	
124	| Key | Action |
125	| --- | --- |
126	| Tab | Move to the alert's actions and dismiss control in reading order. The alert itself is not focusable. |
127	| Enter | Activate the focused dismiss control. |
128	| Space | Activate the focused dismiss control. |
129	
130	## Rationale
131	
132	- **The label is an option of the title part, and dismissible and the dismiss label are options of the dismiss part. Variant and announce stay options of the alert.** Each of the first three shapes one part (ADR 0005). Variant colors the surface and icon, and announce governs how the whole alert reaches assistive technology. The dismiss options keep their names, so the web and React APIs do not change.
133	- **Announcement is its own parameter, off by default, and independent of the variant.** A danger alert present when a view loads should be found by reading, not announced, while a routine success message after an action should be announced politely. Tying urgency to color would get both wrong. Off by default means nothing is announced unless the consumer asks.
134	- **Dismissal hides the alert itself, after a cancelable dismiss event.** Every consumer would otherwise write the same hide step. The cancelable event lets a consumer keep the alert, remove it, or move focus first. Hiding without a fallback for focus would leave keyboard users at the top of the page, so the alert moves focus to its neighbor.
135	- **Alert never hides on its own after a delay.** A timed message can disappear before someone with a screen magnifier, a screen reader, or a slow reading pace finds it (WCAG 2.2.1). Transient notifications that stack over the view are a separate overlay component, not a mode of this one.
136	- **Alert supplies no icon, and the title is not a heading.** Icon supplies no artwork, so the adopter chooses the symbol for each variant and composes Icon. The right heading level depends on the surrounding page, so a consumer who needs a heading puts it in the message.
137	- **The visible title is set by the label parameter, not a title parameter.** Dialog names its visible title label too, so label stays the one name for the visible text that names a component. A title attribute is already a global HTML attribute that shows a browser tooltip, and title is already a property of every element. The anatomy part stays title because it describes the rendered part, not the parameter.
138	- **Alert has no neutral or accent variant.** Every alert reports a status. Info is the neutral case. Brand emphasis without a status is product layout built from tokens, per the compose-or-propose guideline.
139	- **Alert consumes semantic status tokens directly, with spacing primitives.** Tokens ADR 0003. The quiet status surfaces are audited for body text, status content, and borders in both themes, and the focus border and brand text (for a composed Link) are audited against each of them. No semantic spacing role exists, so spacing primitives set padding and gaps. The title uses semantic.typography.title, as in Dialog. The dismiss control borrows the tertiary action hover and pressed fills because it is a low-emphasis action.
140	- **Alert has no disabled, selected, loading, or invalid state.** Alert is a message, not a control. Its danger variant reports an error but is not itself invalid. Composed actions own their own disabled and busy states, and a message about pending work is written as text.
141	- **One size, with no density setting.** The message wraps to the width of its container, and the layout decides that width. A smaller inline status belongs to Badge.
142	- **Alert always has text. The dismiss control is the only icon-only part.** An alert without words would carry meaning by color and symbol alone (text-states-status). The dismiss control shows only a graphic, so its accessible name comes from the dismiss label parameter (dismiss-accessible-name).
143	- **Layout follows the reading direction. Nothing mirrors.** The icon leads and the dismiss control trails in the reading direction. The dismiss graphic is symmetric. Directional artwork in a supplied icon is the adopter's choice, as with Icon.
144	- **Alert does not animate when it appears or hides.** Instant changes satisfy a reduced motion preference without a separate treatment, and an entrance animation would delay reading a message that may also be announced.
145	- **Forced colors keep the boundary and focus through system colors.** The variant fills disappear under forced colors, so the border takes the system text color and focus the system highlight. The words carry the status (text-states-status).
146	
147	## Links

151	- [Badge](component.badge) — Label a status or category on an item in a list or table. Badge is a compact label on an item. Alert is a message in the flow of the page.

156	- [Accordion](component.accordion) — A status message or error people must see. An alert is shown in the flow of the page. Hiding it behind a heading hides the problem.
157	- [Badge](component.badge) — Announce a live status change by itself. Badge sets no live-region role. Alert announces its message when asked to.
158	- [Badge](component.badge) — Explain a status in a sentence or offer an action that resolves it. Badge is a short label. Alert holds a message and actions.
159	- [Card](component.card) — Report the outcome of an action or a condition that affects the view. Alert carries status color and can be announced. A card is neutral content.
160	- [Dialog](component.dialog) — Show a passive status message that needs no response. Blocking the view interrupts the person unnecessarily.
161	- [Progress bar](component.progress-bar) — Report that the task finished or failed. The bar stops at done but does not say what happened. Alert states the outcome and can announce it.
162	- [Spinner](component.spinner) — Report that the work finished or failed. Spinner only says work is happening. Alert states the outcome and can announce it.

701	# Form field
702	
703	Give every form control the same label, hint, error, required, disabled, and form behavior.
704	
705	Text field, Text area, Select, Checkbox, Switch, Radio group, and Slider follow this pattern and
706	inherit the rules above. Keyboard focus and forced colors come from `guideline.accessibility`,
707	which they also follow. Each keeps only the rules about its own control. It narrows a rule where its
708	control differs, such as what its value is, and waives one that cannot apply, with the reason.
709	
710	## Label, hint, and error
711	
712	The label says what the value is. The hint says what the label cannot, such as a format or a
713	consequence. The error says how to fix what was entered. Assistive technology reads the label as the
714	control's name and the hint and error as its description, so each must make sense on its own.
715	
716	## Switch and forms
717	
718	Switch applies its setting immediately, without a separate submit action. It can also submit with a
719	form, so these rules apply to it. Use Checkbox when the choice takes effect only when the form is
720	submitted.
721	
722	## Rules
723	
724	### Content
725	
726	- **MUST** visible-label: Provide a visible label that names the value. Placeholder text is not a label.
727	  - Do: Email address
